story: Fairbanks North Star Borough Ordinance No. 2026-42 proposes a temporary moratorium on land use permits for large-scale data centers through 2027

claims.claim: Fairbanks North Star Borough Ordinance No. 2026-42 is titled An Ordinance Establishing A Temporary Moratorium On Land Use Permits For Large Scale Data Centers.
claims.verbatim: ORDINANCE NO. 2026-42. An Ordinance Establishing A Temporary Moratorium On Land Use Permits For Large Scale Data Centers.
claims.source_outlet: Fairbanks North Star Borough, October 22nd Assembly agenda
claims.notes: Agenda item 17.a. The same title appears in the ordinance text on packet page 520 and in the agenda reproduced on packet page 3 (fileId 13344). Corroborated by Alaska's News Source on October 23rd.

claims.claim: Borough Mayor Grier Hopkins is the sponsor of Ordinance No. 2026-42.
claims.verbatim: (Sponsor: Mayor Hopkins)
claims.source_outlet: Fairbanks North Star Borough, October 22nd Assembly agenda
claims.notes: The ordinance header in the packet (page 520) reads "By : Grier Hopkins, Mayor". Alaska's News Source October 23rd says "Borough Mayor Grier Hopkins has proposed a temporary moratorium".

claims.claim: Ordinance No. 2026-42 was item 17.a on the October 22nd Regular Assembly Meeting agenda, under ordinances to be referred to committees or commissions.
claims.verbatim: 17. CONSIDERATION OF CALENDAR - New Business - Ordinances to be Referred to Committees or Commissions 17.a. *ORDINANCE NO. 2026-42.
claims.source_outlet: Fairbanks North Star Borough, October 22nd Assembly agenda
claims.notes: Meeting was October 22nd at 6 p.m. The asterisk marks a consent agenda item. needs_softening true. No minutes or action memo for October 22nd were published as of October 24th (civicclerk event 5657 lists only Agenda and Agenda Packet), so say the ordinance was on the agenda for referral, not that the referral happened. The ordinance header itself reads "Referred to the Planning Commission: 10/22/2026".

claims.claim: The agenda directs Ordinance No. 2026-42 to the Planning Commission with a recommendation due back in 90 days.
claims.verbatim: (Refer to the Planning Commission with a recommendation due back in 90 days)
claims.source_outlet: Fairbanks North Star Borough, October 22nd Assembly agenda
claims.notes: Verbatim also appears on packet page 3 (showrunner pypdf extract). Independently corroborated by Alaska's News Source October 23rd, "referred to the borough Planning Commission for a recommendation within 90 days."

claims.claim: Under Ordinance No. 2026-42 a facility counts as a large-scale data center if it has an aggregate peak electrical demand of 5 MW or greater.
claims.verbatim: (1) has an aggregate peak electrical demand of five megawatts (5 MW) or greater
claims.source_outlet: Fairbanks North Star Borough, October 22nd Assembly agenda packet
claims.notes: Section 2. text extracted by the showrunner from packet pages 520 to 522 with pypdf; packet too large for WebFetch. The three tests are joined by "or", so meeting any one qualifies. Corroborated by Alaska's News Source October 23rd, "an aggregate peak electrical demand of five megawatts (5 MW) or greater,".

claims.claim: Under Ordinance No. 2026-42 a facility also counts as a large-scale data center if it occupies more than 50,000 square feet of floor area devoted to data center operations.
claims.verbatim: (2) occupies more than 50,000 square feet of floor area devoted to data center operations
claims.source_outlet: Fairbanks North Star Borough, October 22nd Assembly agenda packet
claims.notes: Section 2, the phrase runs across the break between packet pages 521 and 522. text extracted by the showrunner from packet pages 520 to 522 with pypdf; packet too large for WebFetch. Corroborated by Alaska's News Source October 23rd, "data center operations occupying more than 50,000 square feet".

claims.claim: Under Ordinance No. 2026-42 a facility also counts as a large-scale data center if it includes onsite electrical generation of 5 MW or greater.
claims.verbatim: (3) includes onsite electrical generation facilities with a generating capacity of five megawatts (5 MW) or greater.
claims.source_outlet: Fairbanks North Star Borough, October 22nd Assembly agenda packet
claims.notes: Section 2, packet page 522. text extracted by the showrunner from packet pages 520 to 522 with pypdf; packet too large for WebFetch. Corroborated by Alaska's News Source October 23rd, "onsite electricity generation capacity greater than or equal to five megawatts."

claims.claim: While the moratorium is in effect no land use permit applications for a large-scale data center would be accepted and no pending applications approved.
claims.verbatim: no land use permit applications for a large-scale data center shall be accepted, nor pending applications approved, while this moratorium is in effect.
claims.source_outlet: Fairbanks North Star Borough, October 22nd Assembly agenda packet
claims.notes: Section 2, packet page 521, preceded by "Notwithstanding any provision of FNSBC Title 18 to the contrary". text extracted by the showrunner from packet pages 520 to 522 with pypdf; packet too large for WebFetch. Margin line numbers removed from the quote. The ordinance is proposed, not adopted.

claims.claim: The moratorium would run through December 31st, 2027 unless the Assembly ends it sooner or extends it by ordinance.
claims.verbatim: shall be in effect through December 31, 2027, unless terminated sooner or extended by ordinance of the Assembly.
claims.source_outlet: Fairbanks North Star Borough, October 22nd Assembly agenda packet
claims.notes: Section 3, packet page 522. text extracted by the showrunner from packet pages 520 to 522 with pypdf; packet too large for WebFetch. Corroborated by Alaska's News Source October 23rd, "the ordinance as currently written would halt permitting for these structures until December 31, 2027".

claims.claim: The planning director's memo says the moratorium would last through the end of 2027 so the borough can update and adopt its new Comprehensive Plan.
claims.verbatim: impose a moratorium on land use permits for large scale data centers in the Fairbanks North Star Borough through the end of 2027.
claims.source_outlet: Fairbanks North Star Borough, October 22nd Assembly agenda packet
claims.notes: Memo on packet page 519, next sentence reads "This timeline will allow the Borough to update and adopt the new Comprehensive Plan". text extracted by the showrunner from packet pages 519 to 522 with pypdf; packet too large for WebFetch. Consistent with C09.

claims.claim: The ordinance directs the Department of Community Planning to report its findings and recommendations to the Planning Commission within six months of the effective date.
claims.verbatim: present a report on those findings to the Planning Commission with recommendations for the land use regulation of large-scale data centers within six months of the effective date of this ordinance.
claims.source_outlet: Fairbanks North Star Borough, October 22nd Assembly agenda packet
claims.notes: Section 4, packet page 522. text extracted by the showrunner from packet pages 520 to 522 with pypdf; packet too large for WebFetch.

claims.claim: The required study covers impacts on energy usage, air quality, water usage and water quality, and noise pollution.
claims.verbatim: including but not limited to impacts on energy usage, air quality, water usage and water quality, and noise pollution.
claims.source_outlet: Fairbanks North Star Borough, October 22nd Assembly agenda packet
claims.notes: Section 4, packet page 522. The list is "including but not limited to", so the four are a floor, not the full scope. text extracted by the showrunner from packet pages 520 to 522 with pypdf; packet too large for WebFetch.

claims.claim: Ordinance No. 2026-42 would take effect at 5 p.m. on the first Borough business day after its adoption.
claims.verbatim: This ordinance is effective at 5:00 p.m. on the first Borough business day following its adoption.
claims.source_outlet: Fairbanks North Star Borough, October 22nd Assembly agenda packet
claims.notes: Section 5, packet page 522. text extracted by the showrunner from packet pages 520 to 522 with pypdf; packet too large for WebFetch.

claims.claim: Ordinance No. 2026-42 is classified as temporary and would not be codified.
claims.verbatim: This ordinance is not of a general and permanent nature and shall not be codified.
claims.source_outlet: Fairbanks North Star Borough, October 22nd Assembly agenda packet
claims.notes: Section 1, packet page 521. text extracted by the showrunner from packet pages 520 to 522 with pypdf; packet too large for WebFetch.

claims.claim: The ordinance says the borough's Regional Comprehensive Plan was last updated in 2005, before growing demand from artificial intelligence created a need for physical infrastructure.
claims.verbatim: Regional Comprehensive Plan (Comprehensive Plan or Plan) was last updated in 2005, prior to growing demand from artificial intelligence creating a need for physical infrastructure
claims.source_outlet: Fairbanks North Star Borough, October 22nd Assembly agenda packet
claims.notes: First WHEREAS, packet page 520, margin line numbers removed. text extracted by the showrunner from packet pages 520 to 522 with pypdf; packet too large for WebFetch. Independently corroborated by the borough's Comprehensive Plan Update page (https://www.fnsb.gov/1169/Comprehensive-Plan-Update), which says the current plan was "last updated and adopted in 2005" and "has a 20-year planning horizon".

claims.claim: The ordinance says the borough zoning code does not address data centers as a permitted or conditional use.
claims.verbatim: the Borough zoning code does not address data centers as a permitted or conditional use
claims.source_outlet: Fairbanks North Star Borough, October 22nd Assembly agenda packet
claims.notes: First WHEREAS, packet page 520. text extracted by the showrunner from packet pages 520 to 522 with pypdf; packet too large for WebFetch. Alaska's News Source October 23rd reports the mayor says borough code does not currently address zoning for AI data centers.

claims.claim: The ordinance says the Comprehensive Plan update is still in progress and expected to be finalized in early 2027.
claims.verbatim: the Comprehensive Plan update is still in progress and expected to be finalized in early 2027
claims.source_outlet: Fairbanks North Star Borough, October 22nd Assembly agenda packet
claims.notes: needs_softening true. It is a projection, so use "expected to be finalized in early 2027". text extracted by the showrunner from packet pages 520 to 522 with pypdf; packet too large for WebFetch.

claims.claim: Under the present zoning ordinance large-scale data centers would be permitted only in the GU-1 and GU-5 General Use Districts.
claims.verbatim: Under the present zoning ordinance, large -scale data centers would be permitted only in the GU-1 and GU-5 General Use Districts
claims.source_outlet: Fairbanks North Star Borough, October 22nd Assembly agenda packet
claims.notes: WHEREAS on packet page 521. The stray space in "large -scale" is a PDF extraction artifact. text extracted by the showrunner from packet pages 520 to 522 with pypdf; packet too large for WebFetch. This is the ordinance's own reading of current code. Title 18 itself could not be fetched (borough code site returned 403), so GU-1 and GU-5 lot sizes and use tables are unverified.

claims.claim: The ordinance says the General Use Districts allow the widest range of land uses of any zoning district in the borough.
claims.verbatim: The General Use Districts allow for the widest range of land uses of any zoning district designation in the Borough
claims.source_outlet: Fairbanks North Star Borough, October 22nd Assembly agenda packet
claims.notes: WHEREAS on packet page 521. text extracted by the showrunner from packet pages 520 to 522 with pypdf; packet too large for WebFetch.

claims.claim: The ordinance says large data centers could consume a significant share of available electrical power in the borough.
claims.value: significant share of available electrical power
claims.verbatim: Large data centers could have substantial adverse impacts within the Borough, including consuming a significant share of available electrical power
claims.source_outlet: Fairbanks North Star Borough, October 22nd Assembly agenda packet
claims.notes: WHEREAS spanning packet pages 520 and 521. It is the ordinance's stated concern ("could"), so attribute it to the ordinance. text extracted by the showrunner from packet pages 520 to 522 with pypdf; packet too large for WebFetch.

claims.claim: The ordinance names noise from cooling and power equipment as a possible impact of large data centers.
claims.value: noise from cooling and power equipment
claims.verbatim: generating noise from cooling and power equipment
claims.source_outlet: Fairbanks North Star Borough, October 22nd Assembly agenda packet
claims.notes: Same WHEREAS as C20, packet page 521. text extracted by the showrunner from packet pages 520 to 522 with pypdf; packet too large for WebFetch.

claims.claim: The ordinance names degraded air quality from onsite power generation emissions as a possible impact of large data centers.
claims.verbatim: degrading air quality through emissions from onsite power generation facilities
claims.source_outlet: Fairbanks North Star Borough, October 22nd Assembly agenda packet
claims.notes: Same WHEREAS as C20, packet page 521. text extracted by the showrunner from packet pages 520 to 522 with pypdf; packet too large for WebFetch. The ordinance does not mention PM2.5 or nonattainment. See C33 for the EPA status, and keep any link between the two as the deck's own framing.

claims.claim: The ordinance says a temporary pause lets the borough assess power demand, water consumption, noise and land-use compatibility before development proceeds.
claims.verbatim: ensures that development does not proceed before the Borough can fully assess impacts such as power demand, water consumption, noise, and land-use compatibility
claims.source_outlet: Fairbanks North Star Borough, October 22nd Assembly agenda packet
claims.notes: Final WHEREAS, packet page 521, margin line numbers removed. text extracted by the showrunner from packet pages 520 to 522 with pypdf; packet too large for WebFetch.

claims.verbatim: FROM: Kellen Spillman Director Community Planning Department DATE: October 22, 2026 SUBJECT: Ordinance No. 2026-42
claims.source_outlet: Fairbanks North Star Borough, October 22nd Assembly agenda packet
claims.notes: Memo on packet page 519, addressed to Presiding Officer Scott Crass through Mayor Grier Hopkins. text extracted by the showrunner from packet page 519 with pypdf; packet too large for WebFetch. Whitespace between memo fields collapsed in the quote.

claims.notes: Memo on packet page 519. text extracted by the showrunner from packet page 519 with pypdf; packet too large for WebFetch.

claims.claim: Item 9.a on the October 22nd agenda was the Borough Clerk's memorandum on certifying the October 6th Regular Municipal Election.
claims.verbatim: regarding the certification of the Fairbanks North Star Borough October 6, 2026 Regular Municipal Election
claims.source_outlet: Fairbanks North Star Borough, October 22nd Assembly agenda
claims.notes: The memo is from Borough Clerk April Trickey, MMC, and is not on the consent agenda. The quote is a substring returned by the fetch tool, which cut the full item for length.

claims.claim: On August 27th the Assembly adopted Resolution No. 2026-25, its legislative priorities resolution, by a vote of 6-1.
claims.verbatim: VOTE ON MOTION TO ADOPT RESOLUTION NO. 2026-25. Yeses: Guttenberg, Armstrong, LaJiness, Kelly, Roach, Reeves Noes: Rotermund MOTION PASSED 6 Yeses, 1 Noes
claims.source_outlet: Fairbanks North Star Borough, August 27th Assembly minutes
claims.notes: BACKGROUND, outside the window. Read from the scanned minutes PDF, page 7. Title on page 4 is "A Resolution Identifying And Supporting Legislative Priorities". Assemblymember Tammie Wilson was excused for a conflict and Scott Crass was excused from the meeting. Adoption is also confirmed by the August 27th action memo (fileId 13145). The scout-cited Alaska's News Source September story does not carry the vote or resolution number.

claims.claim: Residents testifying on Resolution 2026-25 spoke in support of its legislative priority for a moratorium on data center development in Alaska.
claims.value: Moratorium on Data Center Development in Alaska
claims.verbatim: spoke in support of the Legislative Priority regarding a Moratorium on Data Center Development in Alaska.
claims.source_outlet: Fairbanks North Star Borough, August 27th Assembly minutes
claims.notes: BACKGROUND. The phrase recurs for many speakers on minutes pages 5 and 6. Corroborated by Alaska Public Media October 15th, which says the borough assembly passed a resolution in August asking the state to ask the Alaska Legislature to impose a moratorium on data centers. The scout detail that the request was limited to state or municipal land was NOT found and is killed.

claims.claim: Assemblymember Brett Rotermund cast the only no vote on Resolution 2026-25.
claims.verbatim: Noes: Rotermund
claims.source_outlet: Fairbanks North Star Borough, August 27th Assembly minutes
claims.notes: BACKGROUND. Minutes page 7, and his full name appears in the roll call on page 1. The resolution covered many priorities, so do not frame his vote as a vote against a moratorium.

claims.claim: Mayor Hopkins told Alaska's News Source that residents asked for a moratorium during the legislative priorities hearings.
claims.verbatim: We heard it during the legislative priorities hearings, that people want a moratorium until we can figure out
claims.source_outlet: Alaska's News Source
claims.notes: Story by Alex Bengel, published October 23rd at 5.18 p.m. AKDT although the URL path says 10/24. The quote is a verbatim substring, and the fetch tool cut the sentence after "figure out", so do not complete it.

claims.claim: Assembly member Tammie Wilson told Alaska's News Source she was glad the borough was being proactive instead of reactive.
claims.verbatim: I'm really glad to see that we're being proactive instead of reactive,
claims.source_outlet: Alaska's News Source
claims.notes: The same story reports Assembly member Brett Rotermund had not yet decided (paraphrase only, no quote verified). Apostrophes may be typographic on the live page.

claims.claim: The borough's Comprehensive Plan Update page schedules a Planning Commission work session on the final plan for October 27th, followed by a public hearing in November.
claims.verbatim: October 27, 2026: Planning Commission work session on final plan
claims.source_outlet: Fairbanks North Star Borough Community Planning
claims.notes: The page is undated, so the date shown is the fetch date. Next schedule line is "November 2026: Planning Commission public hearing on final plan". The page gives no Assembly adoption date, consistent with C17's early 2027. The page does not mention data centers. The borough calendar also lists an October 27th Planning Commission work session at 6.05 p.m. needs_softening true. These are scheduled events, so write "scheduled".

claims.claim: EPA lists the Fairbanks, AK area as nonattainment for the 2006 PM2.5 standard with a Serious classification.
claims.verbatim: Fairbanks, AK | AK | Nonattainment | A | Serious | 1 | 87,456 | 10
claims.source_outlet: U.S. EPA Green Book
claims.notes: BACKGROUND. Page title "PM-2.5 (2006) Designated Area/State Information", and "Data is current as of September 30, 2026". The verbatim reproduces the table row cells with pipes as separators. Columns are Area Name, State, Current Status, a sort letter, Current Classification, No. Counties, 2010 Population (87,456), EPA Region. The nonattainment area is the Fairbanks and North Pole area, not the whole borough, so do not say the entire borough. The Alaska DEC page returned 403, so no second source was found. It is primary, so it is acceptable.

claims.claim: Golden Valley Electric Association issued its first Energy Emergency Alert on October 12th.
claims.verbatim: Yesterday, GVEA issued an Energy Emergency Alert (EEA) for the first time.
claims.source_outlet: Golden Valley Electric Association
claims.notes: The release is dated October 13th, so "yesterday" is October 12th, a Monday. Corroborated by Alaska Public Media October 15th, which says GVEA "issued its first-ever energy emergency alert on Monday." Alaska's News Source October 14th does not call it the first and quotes a spokesperson describing the alerts as a new way of communicating.

claims.claim: GVEA's October 12th alert was a Level 2 alert.
claims.verbatim: required us to issue a Level 2 alert sooner
claims.source_outlet: Golden Valley Electric Association
claims.notes: Corroborated by Alaska's News Source October 14th (Alex Bengel), which describes the email as level two of a four-level system asking members to conserve and prepare for possible outages through Wednesday.

claims.claim: GVEA's Level 1 Energy Advisory means available generation reserves are below 38 MW.
claims.verbatim: Available generation reserves are below 38 MW and are not expected to recover in the next two hours.
claims.source_outlet: Golden Valley Electric Association
claims.notes: Evergreen page whose status line read October 20th, 8.15 a.m. Corroborated by Alaska's News Source October 14th, "level one means there are less than 38 megawatts in reserve".

claims.claim: GVEA's Level 2 Energy Watch means available generation reserves are below 15 MW.
claims.verbatim: Available generation reserves are below 15 MW and are not expected to recover within two hours.
claims.source_outlet: Golden Valley Electric Association
claims.notes: Level 2 instruction on the page is "Conserve now and prepare for possible outages." Corroborated by Alaska's News Source October 14th, "level two represents less than 15 megawatts."

claims.claim: At GVEA's Level 3 Energy Warning the controlled load shed program begins because generation reserves are unavailable.
claims.verbatim: CONTROLLED LOAD SHED PROGRAM INITIATED. Generation reserves are unavailable and are not expected to recover within 30 minutes.
claims.source_outlet: Golden Valley Electric Association
claims.notes: Level 3 was not reached in the October 12th event per the sources fetched.

claims.claim: A GVEA spokesperson said a Level 3 load shed would rotate through zones in outages of 30 to 60 minutes.
claims.verbatim: we would go through a certain number of zones for 30 to 60-minute outages
claims.source_outlet: Alaska's News Source
claims.notes: Published October 14th at 5.26 p.m. AKDT by Alex Bengel, though the URL path says 10/15. The same article says GVEA has 13 zones (paraphrase). GVEA's own October 13th release also describes rotating outages of 30 to 60 minutes through designated zones.

claims.claim: GVEA said two of its generating units were offline for planned maintenance when a third went offline unexpectedly.
claims.verbatim: Right now, two of our generating units are offline for planned maintenance.
claims.source_outlet: Golden Valley Electric Association
claims.notes: The third unit's unexpected outage is from the release as paraphrased by the fetch tool. It is corroborated by Alaska's News Source October 14th, "one of the utility's generation units going offline while two others were undergoing scheduled maintenance." Neither source names the failed unit.

claims.claim: Interior Secretary Doug Burgum spoke at a Fairbanks Chamber of Commerce event on October 14th.
claims.verbatim: Interior Secretary Doug Burgum speaks at a Fairbanks Chamber of Commerce event on Oct. 14, 2026.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Public Media (KUAC)
claims.notes: The quote is a photo caption. Story by Shelby Herbert, KUAC, published October 15th.

claims.claim: Burgum said people were knocking on the door wanting to drop 10 billion on a data center without tax breaks.
claims.verbatim: We have people knocking on our door that want to drop 10 billion on a data center, and they don't want any tax breaks.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Public Media (KUAC)
claims.notes: The page prints "10 billion" with no dollar sign, so a quote must read 10 billion. Dollars are implied, and a paraphrase may say $10 billion. needs_softening true. It is an unverified claim by Burgum about unnamed developers, so attribute it to him.

claims.claim: Alaska Public Media reports that Alaska has seen proposals for as many as 15 data centers, including on military land.
claims.verbatim: Alaska has seen proposals for as many as 15 data centers, including on military land near Railbelt and Interior communities.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Public Media (KUAC)
claims.notes: This is the reporter's statement, NOT a Burgum quote. Attribute it to Alaska Public Media. needs_softening true. Say "as many as 15".

claims.claim: In July state officials received more than 500 public comments on a proposed North Slope data center and power plant.
claims.verbatim: In July, state officials received more than 500 public comments on a proposed North Slope data center and power plant.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Public Media (KUAC)
claims.notes: BACKGROUND event (July), reported in window. This is the reporter's statement, not Burgum's.

claims.claim: Democratic gubernatorial candidate Jonathan Kreiss-Tomkins said of data centers that he thinks Alaska should pause.
claims.verbatim: I think we should pause
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Public Media (KUAC)
claims.notes: The article calls him the sole Democratic candidate in the governor's race. He attended Burgum's speech. Next verbatim words are "We should make sure that we have laws in place that protect the public interest. And then, in a thoughtful way, development can proceed." Quote only these exact words.

claims.claim: In a commentary Gwen Holdmann wrote that the Alaska Intertie carried roughly 540,000 megawatt-hours in 2014.
claims.verbatim: In 2014, the intertie carried roughly 540,000 megawatt-hours
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Beacon (commentary by Gwen Holdmann)
claims.notes: Verified against the full text in https://alaskabeacon.com/feed/ (feed pubDate Wed, 21 Oct 2026 23.35 UTC). The article URL itself returns 403 to the fetcher. Commentary titled "Cook Inlet's gas shortage has become Fairbanks' diesel bill". Opinion piece, so attribute to Holdmann. Her affiliation is not stated in the feed and was not verified.

claims.claim: Holdmann wrote that the 2014 intertie flow equaled more than 40% of GVEA's annual electricity sales.
claims.verbatim: an amount equivalent to more than 40%
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Beacon (commentary by Gwen Holdmann)
claims.notes: Verified via https://alaskabeacon.com/feed/. The sentence continues "of GVEA's annual electricity sales", possibly with a typographic apostrophe. Commentary, attribute to Holdmann.

claims.claim: Holdmann wrote that economy-power purchases over the intertie have fallen to essentially zero since early 2025.
claims.verbatim: But since early 2025, those economy-power purchases have fallen to essentially zero.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Beacon (commentary by Gwen Holdmann)
claims.notes: Verified via https://alaskabeacon.com/feed/. Commentary, attribute to Holdmann. needs_softening true. Use "Holdmann wrote".

claims.claim: Holdmann wrote that in 2014 the older diesel-fired turbines at North Pole supplied only about 3% of GVEA's electricity.
claims.verbatim: the older diesel-fired turbines at North Pole supplied only about 3% of its electricity
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Beacon (commentary by Gwen Holdmann)
claims.notes: Verified via https://alaskabeacon.com/feed/. "its" refers to GVEA per context. Commentary, attribute to Holdmann.

claims.claim: Holdmann wrote that by 2025 those diesel turbines were supplying 15% of GVEA's electricity.
claims.verbatim: By 2025, those diesel turbines were supplying 15% of its electricity.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Beacon (commentary by Gwen Holdmann)
claims.notes: Verified via https://alaskabeacon.com/feed/. A fivefold rise from about 3% (C49) is arithmetic on her figures. Commentary, attribute to Holdmann.

claims.claim: Holdmann wrote that residential electricity rates climbed above 37 cents per kilowatt-hour this past summer.
claims.verbatim: residential electricity rates climbed above 37 cents per kilowatt-hour
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Beacon (commentary by Gwen Holdmann)
claims.notes: Verified via https://alaskabeacon.com/feed/. In context these are Fairbanks (GVEA) rates during the summer, but the fetched excerpt did not name the utility in the same sentence. needs_softening true. Write "Fairbanks residential rates topped 37 cents per kilowatt-hour this summer, Holdmann wrote".

claims.claim: On October 21st the USGS released an assessment estimating 96 trillion cubic feet of technically recoverable undiscovered natural gas on Alaska's North Slope.
claims.verbatim: The U.S. Geological Survey released an assessment estimating 96 trillion cubic feet of technically recoverable, undiscovered
claims.source_outlet: U.S. Department of the Interior
claims.notes: Release datelined RESTON, Va., 10/21/2026, headline "USGS Releases Assessment of Undiscovered Natural Gas Resources in Alaska's North Slope". The page does NOT use the word "mean", give the 17.3 to 276.6 range, the 2008 estimate or years of US consumption. needs_softening true. It is an estimate of undiscovered resources, so write "estimated".

claims.claim: Interior says the 96 trillion cubic feet estimate is nearly three times the roughly 35 trillion cubic feet of proven North Slope gas reserves.
claims.verbatim: This is nearly three times the roughly 35 trillion cubic feet (TCFG) of proven gas reserves on the North Slope.
claims.source_outlet: U.S. Department of the Interior
claims.notes: Sanity check passes, 96 divided by 35 is about 2.7.

claims.claim: Taiwan's Economic Affairs Ministry said it would invest up to $4.4 billion in the Alaska LNG pipeline project.
claims.verbatim: will invest up to $4.4 billion in the pipeline project
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Beacon via Alaska Public Media
claims.notes: Story by James Brooks, published October 15th. Independently corroborated by AP via Alaska Public Media October 14th, "with an estimated maximum investment of $4.4 billion". needs_softening true. Beacon says terms and size are subject to further negotiations, so write "up to".

claims.claim: Taiwan is preparing to buy as much as 30% of the Alaska LNG pipeline's production.
claims.verbatim: preparing to buy as much as 30% of the pipeline's production
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Beacon via Alaska Public Media
claims.notes: AP October 14th quotes Trump, "Taiwan has just agreed to buy 30% of the gas coming off the pipeline for the next 20 years." AP notes Taiwan's statement did not specify a number of years. needs_softening true. Use "as much as 30%", and attribute the 20 years only to Trump.

claims.claim: Taiwan plans to buy 6.6 million U.S. tons of liquefied natural gas a year from the Alaska project once extraction starts.
claims.verbatim: Taiwan plans to buy 6.6 million U.S. tons of liquefied natural gas annually from a U.S. project once extraction starts
claims.source_outlet: The Associated Press via Alaska Public Media
claims.notes: Beacon October 15th says "6 million metric tons of gas per year". Sanity check passes, 6 million metric tons is about 6.6 million short tons. Do not mix units on one slide.

claims.claim: Taiwan's ministry said Alaska gas would start supplying the island in 2032 at the earliest if the project stays on schedule.
claims.verbatim: it is expected to start supporting the island's natural gas supply in 2032 at the earliest
claims.source_outlet: The Associated Press via Alaska Public Media
claims.notes: needs_softening true. It is a projection, so write "2032 at the earliest".

claims.claim: The Alaska LNG project centers on an 807-mile pipeline from the North Slope to an export terminal.
claims.verbatim: an 807-mile pipeline connecting Alaska's North Slope to a liquefied natural gas export terminal
claims.source_outlet: The Associated Press via Alaska Public Media
claims.notes: Single wire-service source. Long-standing project figure, low dispute risk.

claims.claim: President Trump said the Alaska LNG pipeline is now a U.S. Federal Government Project.
claims.verbatim: is now a U.S. Federal Government Project
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Beacon via Alaska Public Media
claims.notes: AP October 14th places Trump at a campaign rally in Wasilla on Tuesday, October 13th (photo caption). The AP piece does not use the federal project phrase. needs_softening true. What federal status means is undefined (ADN October 20th asked what it means, not fetched), so attribute it to Trump and do not state it as fact.

claims.claim: Official estimates put the Alaska LNG project's cost at $44.5 billion to $54.5 billion.
claims.verbatim: Official estimates state that the project will cost between $44.5 billion to $54.5 billion.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Beacon via Alaska Public Media
claims.notes: Single source fetched. It is an estimate range, so write "estimated".

claims.claim: The private developer Glenfarne owns seventy-five percent of the Alaska LNG pipeline project.
claims.verbatim: Seventy-five percent of the pipeline project is currently owned by the private developer Glenfarne
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Beacon via Alaska Public Media
claims.notes: The scout's AGDC 25 percent share was not confirmed on a fetched page. Do not state it.

claims.claim: Trump has touted a $54 billion South Korean investment in the Alaska pipeline, while South Korean officials have been more cautious.
claims.verbatim: Trump had similarly touted a $54 billion investment from South Korea in the Alaska pipeline.
claims.source_outlet: The Associated Press via Alaska Public Media
claims.notes: needs_softening true. AP adds that South Korean officials said they needed to assess commercial viability first, and Beacon October 15th gives no dollar figure for Korea. Present it only as Trump's claim. The scout note that the Beacon called it false was not verified on a fetched page.

The USGS North Slope gas assessment and the Alaska LNG Taiwan statements (C52 to C62)

killed.claim: Resolution 2026-25 requested a data center moratorium on state or municipal land.
killed.why: Not found in the August 27th minutes, the Alaska's News Source September story or Alaska Public October 15th. Only a moratorium on data center development in Alaska is supported (C28).

killed.claim: Alaska's News Source September 2nd as the source for the 6-1 vote on Resolution 2026-25.
killed.why: That page has no resolution number, vote count or date. The vote is re-sourced to the primary August 27th minutes (C27).

killed.claim: GVEA's October 12th alert was its first-ever, sourced to Alaska's News Source October 14th.
killed.why: That article does not say first or give the date. The claim survives only on GVEA's own October 13th release and Alaska Public October 15th (C34).

killed.claim: The Air Force offered about 4,700 acres across JBER, Eielson and Clear for AI data center enhanced use leases.
killed.why: af.mil returned 403 on both the article and print URLs, and no second source was reached. Unverified.

killed.claim: GU-1 and GU-5 minimum lot sizes and permitted use descriptions from FNSB Title 18.
killed.why: fnsb.borough.codes, municode and codepublishing all returned 403. Only the ordinance's own statements survive (C18, C19).

killed.claim: Borough zoning does or does not reach federal military land at Eielson.
killed.why: No fetched source addresses it. Do not state either way.

killed.claim: The USGS 96 Tcf figure is a mean, with a range of 17.3 to 276.6 Tcf, about 3 years of US consumption, against a 2008 estimate of 119.15 Tcf.
killed.why: None of these appear on the DOI release, the only page fetched. Write "estimated 96 trillion cubic feet" and leave out the range and comparisons.

killed.claim: The Alaska Beacon called the $54 billion Korean investment claim false.
killed.why: The Beacon October 15th story fetched gives no Korean dollar figure and no such characterization.

killed.claim: AGDC owns 25 percent of Alaska LNG.
killed.why: Not on any fetched page. Only Glenfarne's 75 percent is verified (C61).

killed.claim: Burgum said "$10 billion" with a dollar sign.
killed.why: The page prints "10 billion". Quoted copy must use 10 billion (C42).

killed.claim: The 15 data center proposals and the 500 plus comments are Burgum's remarks.
killed.why: Both are the reporter's statements in Alaska Public, not Burgum quotes. They are re-attributed in C43 and C44.

killed.claim: Gwen Holdmann's professional title or affiliation.
killed.why: The Beacon feed carries only her byline. No affiliation was verified, so attribute only to her commentary.
